title: Approvals and Accountability
before:
1. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. No other role carries this overall accountability.

2. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. The shift supervisor exercises approval authority only within that shift and escalates all matters beyond the defined thresholds to the warehouse manager.

3. Under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results. No stocktake is closed, posted or communicated to the client until that sign-off is obtained. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy through cycle counts, recounts and adjustments, but they do not hold sign-off authority.

4. Under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse manager approval. The threshold is applied as follows:
  a) The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR.
  b) The warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR.
Submit the damage report, value calculation and photographs to the relevant approver before scrapping, disposal or system write-off. Do not split a single damage event to remain below the threshold.

5. Under PR-07 Returns handling, the shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap, but the disposition takes effect only after shift supervisor approval. Do not move inspected returns back to stock until approval is recorded.

6. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime. Request overtime in advance with reason, hours and staff required. Do not work or record overtime hours without written approval from the warehouse manager.

7. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Submit all injuries, near misses, equipment damage and procedural deviations to the shift supervisor on duty. Carry out corrective actions assigned from that review and close the report only when the shift supervisor confirms completion.

8. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators. No operator may drive counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks or other MHE until the warehouse manager has issued authorisation. Maintain the authorisation register centrally and withdraw authorisation where training or medical requirements lapse.

9. Accountability for communication at shift change rests with the outgoing and incoming shift supervisors under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Complete the handover record, note open approvals, pending write-offs and outstanding incident reviews, and obtain acknowledgement from the incoming shift supervisor.

title: Shift Leadership and Dock Control
before:
1. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. The role provides continuous floor leadership across both operating windows.

2. Shift coverage is as follows:
 a. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday.
 b. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
 Each shift has a designated shift supervisor accountable for personnel deployment, task allocation and first response to operational and safety incidents during that shift.

3. The shift supervisor holds the following decision authorities on the floor:
 a. Approve damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR.
 b. Approve the final disposition of inspected returns following inspection in Zone F.
 c. Review every incident report raised on shift.
 Escalations above these thresholds pass to the warehouse manager under Chapter 2.2.

4. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. The function controls all vehicle movements to and from the building.

5. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Allocation follows the fixed door designation:
 a. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving.
 b. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch.
 No carrier may occupy a door without a scheduled assignment from the dispatcher.

6. Coordination between the shift supervisor and the dispatcher is mandatory at shift start, mid-shift and before end-of-shift handover:
 a. The dispatcher confirms the inbound and outbound door plan for doors 1-4 and 5-8.
 b. The shift supervisor confirms staffing for unloading in Zone A, replenishment and picking in Zones B and C, and staging in Zone D.
 c. Both roles align on priorities for delayed carriers, labour constraints and incident impacts.

7. During live operations, the shift supervisor retains authority for floor safety and manning, while the dispatcher retains authority for the door schedule. If a safety incident requires a door to be closed or a load to be held, the shift supervisor directs the immediate action and the dispatcher re-books the affected time slot.

8. All releases of outbound loads from Zone D remain with the dispatcher. Forklift operators and pickers must not release or dispatch a load without dispatcher authorisation, even when staging is complete.

title: Disposition and Write-Offs
before:

2. Hold all goods awaiting a disposition decision in the quarantine area in Zone F. Do not move goods to bulk storage, picking or dispatch while the decision is pending.
3. Keep the quarantine area segregated within Zone F, which holds the value-added services area, and maintain clear identification of each pallet or unit under review.
4. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap. Record the proposal in the WMS with the inspection notes and photographs.
5. Returns are inspected BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision. Do not action the proposal until inspection is closed and the proposal is logged.
6. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns under PR-07 Returns handling. Obtain that approval before releasing goods from quarantine.
7. Execute the approved disposition exactly as instructed:
  a. Restock approved goods to the assigned storage location.

  c. Move scrap goods to the scrap holding point and book the write-off in the WMS.

12. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results. Do not apply that authority to returns or damaged-goods decisions, which follow the thresholds in this section.

title: Adjustments and Recounts
before:
1. Apply this section to every variance found during PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. Treat cycle-count variances and full stocktake variances under the same control.

2. Execute a recount before any adjustment. A second count happens before any stock adjustment is posted. Do not post the adjustment from the first count alone.

3. Assign accountability for accuracy to the stock controller. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments. Direct all count sheets, recount requests and system adjustments to the stock controller for verification.

4. Trigger recounts from daily cycle counts. Cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule. Raise a recount immediately when the first count does not match the system quantity, when the location holds damaged stock, or when the picker reports a short pick.

5. Isolate the location pending recount. Keep the pallet or bin on hold in the system. Do not move, pick, replenish or dispatch stock from that location until the recount is complete.

6. Perform the recount independently. Use the original count method and re-scan each item. Record the second quantity, the counter name and the time on the recount form and return it to the stock controller.

7. Verify and decide on adjustment. Instruct the stock controller to compare the first and second counts, investigate system movements, and determine the correct on-hand quantity. Post the stock adjustment in the WMS only after the recount result is verified.

8. Link stock adjustments that create damaged-goods write-offs to the approval threshold. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval.

9. Route write-off approvals as follows. Submit write-offs up to 500 EUR to the shift supervisor for approval. Submit write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager for approval. Do not scrap, donate or remove stock from the system without the applicable approval recorded.

10. Close stocktake results under final sign-off control. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results. Withhold system release and financial posting of annual stocktake adjustments until that sign-off is recorded for PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.

title: 4.2 Damaged Goods, Quarantine and Returns
before:

Move any damaged, leaking or suspected non-conforming stock to the quarantine area in Zone F on the same day you identify it. Do not leave damaged pallets in bulk storage, picking or dispatch staging.
Zone F holds the value-added services area and contains the quarantine area. All goods awaiting disposition under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling must remain there until a decision is recorded.

2. Apply PR-09 Damaged-goods handling for every incident.
Tag the stock, photograph the damage, retain labels and log the quantity, location and reason in the WMS. Keep the physical stock in the quarantine area in Zone F while awaiting approval.
Do not rework, restock or scrap any item until the approver has signed the disposition.

3. Observe write-off approval thresholds.
Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval. Forward the request with photos, counts and value calculation to the warehouse manager for final decision.

4. Receive and inspect returns under PR-07 Returns handling.
Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery. Reject returns outside this window unless the shift supervisor instructs otherwise.
Returns are inspected in Zone F. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap.

5. Follow inspection then disposition order.
Returns are inspected BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision. Complete the inspection fully before you record a disposition.
Verify the return against delivery documentation and the 14-day window, open and count, examine condition, photograph damage and retain labels, then propose restock, rework or scrap. Record the inspection outcome in the WMS while the goods are still in Zone F.

6. Obtain approval before moving inspected returns.
The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns. Do not move goods to bulk storage, picking, or the value-added services area for rework until the shift supervisor has approved and the WMS entry is posted.
Hold scrap stock in the quarantine area in Zone F until approved for disposal. Route approved rework goods only as directed for Zone F.

title: 1.1 Warehouse Manager - Site Accountability and Final Sign-offs
before:
1.1 Warehouse Manager - Site Accountability and Final Sign-offs

1. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
2. The scope of accountability covers the warehouse floor of 6,000 m2, the high-bay racking providing 2,400 pallet positions and the building with 8 dock doors.
3. Site operations run over two shifts, and the warehouse manager retains overall accountability for both:
   a. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday.
   b. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

4. The warehouse manager holds exclusive sign-off authorities that cannot be delegated:
   a. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.
   b. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
   c. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.
   d. The warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

5. The threshold for damaged-goods escalation is fixed. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, and requests above that value are forwarded for final decision by the warehouse manager.

6. The warehouse manager owns compliance with sequencing controls for safety and inventory integrity:
   a. Under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, ensure a second count happens before any stock adjustment is posted.
   b. Under PR-14 Emergency evacuation, ensure roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.

7. The warehouse manager is responsible for periodic governance and documented assurance:
   a. Ensure a full wall-to-wall stocktake runs once a year and withhold release of the WMS for normal operations until sign-off is recorded.
   b. Ensure racking gets a documented safety inspection every month.
   c. Ensure an evacuation drill runs every quarter under PR-14 Emergency evacuation.

8. The warehouse manager maintains oversight of shift governance. PR-15 End-of-shift handover is applied at every change of supervisor, and the warehouse manager reviews handover records and incident outcomes to confirm that staffing, operational and safety issues are closed between Shift 1 and Shift 2.
9. The warehouse manager provides final accountability for site safety, including adherence to inventory adjustment discipline, evacuation discipline and authorisation controls for personnel and overtime.

  1) Ensure racking gets a documented safety inspection every month and defects are quarantined and reported.

title: 3.1 Damaged Goods and Quarantine Handling
before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. shall handle all damaged, leaking or suspected non-conforming stock under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and shall move such stock to quarantine on the same day it is identified.

2. All goods awaiting disposition under PR-09 shall be held in the quarantine area in Zone F until inspection, approval and posting are complete. Zone F holds the value-added services area and is the sole quarantine location for damaged goods pending disposition.

3. The quarantine process shall be controlled as follows:
  a) The shift supervisor who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response shall be notified immediately of any damage and shall direct placement into the quarantine area in Zone F and review the related reports.
  b) The warehouse manager who is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs shall retain final authority for write-offs above threshold and for overall compliance of quarantine handling.
  c) No quarantined stock shall be moved to bulk storage, picking or dispatch staging without recorded approval under PR-09.

4. Write-off approvals for damaged goods shall follow defined financial thresholds:
  a) The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR.
  b) Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, and the warehouse manager approves such cases.
  c) Harborwick shall not process any write-off above 500 EUR without that approval recorded in the system.

5. Where damaged goods include hazmat, Harborwick shall stage and store such stock only inside the hazmat cage in Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2 and shall contain no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat at one time. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg, therefore the hazmat cage holds at most 4 full-weight pallets. Harborwick commits to enforce this limit and to reject or re-allocate any quantity that would exceed it, reporting the condition immediately.

6. Harborwick shall maintain traceability of all quarantined stock in Zone F, including photographic evidence where required, WMS posting of inspection outcomes, and retention of labels for audit. Disposition to restock, rework or scrap shall only occur after the applicable approver under paragraph 4 has authorised it.
